grades.quote: The operation of WFI must be unaffected by the global interrupt bits in `mstatus` (MIE and SIE) and the delegation register `mideleg` (i.e., the hart must resume if a locally enabled interrupt becomes pending, even if it has been delegated to a less-privileged mode), but should honor the individual interrupt enables (e.g, MTIE)
grades.reason: WFI section explains how pending interrupts, individual enables (e.g. MTIE), global enables (MIE/SIE) and delegation interact for WFI wakeup. It is useful but WFI-specific, not the general delivery rule.

grades.quote: An interrupt _i_ will trap to HS-mode whenever all of the following are true: (a) either the current operating mode is HS-mode and the SIE bit in the `sstatus` register is set, or the current operating mode has less privilege than HS-mode; (b) bit _i_ is set in both `sip` and `sie` , or in both `hip` and `hie` ; and (c) bit _i_ is not set in `hideleg` .
grades.reason: This gives an explicit rule for HS-mode trapping. It combines the current privilege mode, the global SIE enable, the pending and enable bits (sip/sie or hip/hie), and delegation (hideleg).

grades.quote: Bits `hip` .VSSIP and `hie` .VSSIE are the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits for VS-level software interrupts. VSSIP in `hip` is an alias (writable) of the same bit in `hvip` .
grades.reason: This passage describes how the VS-level pending bits in hip are composed and gives the HS-mode interrupt priority order. It does not cover how pending bits, enables and global enables interact for delivery, so it is auxiliary only.
